newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds under pressure on rate hike, auction.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds under pressure on rate hike, auction.

text.p: Greek fixed coupon bonds and FRNs had come under renewed selling pressure shedding 50 to 100 basis points in terms of price, haunted by rising interbank rates and the auction schedule announced on Thursday, dealers said.
"It is a sell-off sparked by rising interbank rates and the announced auction plan," said a dealer at a private bank. "I am afraid it is going to continue in the afternoon when U.S. markets open."
FRN prices have shed 80 to 100 basis points this morning and fixed coupon bonds keep on sliding, the dealer said.
Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis made public on Thursday the state's indicative borrowing schedule programme for the rest of 1997. An auction of seven-year FRNs is planned for June 26.
Dealers said the market expected to see fewer auctions of FRNs in the rest of the year than those showing up in the plan.
Greek depos and forex forwards opened firmer across-the-board with the rise more accentuated in short tenors, traders said.
"Liquidity was tight and got worse after players sought funding for FRNs on Thursday following the announcement of the FRN auction," said a dealer.
Ecu/drachma was holding its ground trading slightly higher than 310, forex dealers said.

"Support for the drachma is underpinned by higher interbank rates," a forex dealer at a foreign bank said. "It is quiet so far with ecu/drachma around 310.03/08." --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
